rows.text: Mutate stacks a pile of creatures into one body, and every "whenever this creature mutates" trigger you have already stacked fires AGAIN each time you add another. So the fourth mutate is not one trigger, it is four or five: draw a card, destroy an artifact, destroy a noncreature permanent, fetch a land, and put a free permanent onto the battlefield. The whole deck is about growing that pile fast and making sure one removal spell cannot eat it.

rows.name: Illuna, Apex of Wishes
rows.text: 6/6 flying trample, and every mutate digs until it finds a nonland permanent and puts it onto the battlefield FREE. Cast her for her mutate cost, not her mana cost, whenever there is a legal base.
Mutate does not cause an enter-the-battlefield trigger. The creature was already there — it just changed. Plan around that: your payoffs here are "whenever this mutates", not "when this enters".

rows.name: Auspicious Starrix
rows.text: exiles until it finds X permanent cards, where X is how many times IT has mutated. The third mutate onto a Starrix pile puts three free permanents onto the battlefield.

rows.name: Dreamtail Heron
rows.text: a card on every subsequent mutate.

rows.name: Gemrazer
rows.text: an artifact or enchantment destroyed on every subsequent mutate. Repeatable Naturalize is not something green usually gets.

rows.name: Sawtusk Demolisher
rows.text: any noncreature permanent destroyed, every mutate.

rows.name: Migratory Greathorn
rows.text: a land every mutate, which pays for the next one.

rows.name: Lore Drakkis
rows.text: buys back an instant or sorcery each time, so your protection spells recur.

rows.name: Pouncing Shoreshark
rows.text: bounces a creature each mutate, and it has FLASH — mutate at instant speed in response to a blocker or a removal spell.

rows.name: Cloudpiercer
rows.text: a loot on each mutate, which finds the next piece.

rows.name: Porcuparrot
rows.text: taps to deal damage equal to the number of times it has mutated. A four-deep pile is a repeatable four-damage removal spell every turn.

rows.name: Sea-Dasher Octopus
rows.text: mutate it on for {1}{U} and the pile draws a card on every connection.
The pile's weakness is obvious: one Swords to Plowshares answers eight cards. Start on a hexproof body and that stops being possible.

rows.name: Slippery Bogle
rows.text: one mana, hexproof, non-Human. The ideal base.

rows.name: Gladecover Scout
rows.text: the second copy.

rows.name: Venomthrope
rows.text: hexproof, flying and deathtouch, so the pile inherits evasion and an unblockable clock.

rows.name: Tamiyo's Safekeeping

rows.name: Legolas's Quick Reflexes
rows.text: split second, so it cannot be responded to at all.

rows.name: Veil of Summer
rows.text: one mana that beats blue and black removal outright, and draws.

rows.name: Frenzied Baloth
rows.text: your creature spells cannot be countered — including every mutate.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free, and it points their removal somewhere else.
If the pile does die, remember Illuna can go back to the command zone instead of the graveyard. The rest of the pile is gone, but the commander is not.

rows.name: Animar, Soul of Elements
rows.text: every creature spell you cast is another counter and another discount. Mutate spells are creature spells, so a few turns in they cost nothing at all.

rows.name: Pollywog Symbiote
rows.text: mutate spells cost one less, and each one you cast filters a card.

rows.name: Radagast of Rhosgobel
rows.text: the first creature spell each turn costs {2} less and can be cast as though it had flash. Mutate on their end step.

rows.name: Delighted Halfling

rows.name: Utopia Sprawl

rows.text: two untapped Forests, which is a four-mana turn out of nowhere.

rows.name: Birds of Paradise
rows.text: turn-one acceleration in a deck that wants to start mutating on turn three.

rows.name: Season of Growth
rows.text: every mutate spell TARGETS a creature you control, so every single one draws a card. Two mana.

rows.name: Beast Whisperer

rows.name: Temur Ascendancy
rows.text: haste for the whole board — which matters because a freshly grown pile wants to attack immediately — plus a card for every big creature that enters.

rows.name: Return of the Wildspeaker
rows.text: draws cards equal to the greatest power among your non-Human creatures. On a real pile that is eight or more, at instant speed. The other mode is a team pump for the kill.

rows.name: Toski, Bearer of Secrets
rows.text: uncounterable, indestructible, and it draws on every connection.

rows.name: Rhystic Study

rows.name: Mystic Remora
rows.text: the first four turns, it is the best card in the deck.

rows.name: Sylvan Library
rows.text: with this much selection, paying life for the extra cards is nearly always right.

rows.name: Scroll Rack
rows.text: swaps a hand of dead cards for the top of your library, and it is exceptional alongside Sylvan Library.

rows.name: Sensei's Divining Top

rows.name: Parcelbeast

rows.name: Pongify

rows.text: cheap in a full board — use it while the pile is hexproof and indestructible, or before you commit.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: counter their wrath and spend the mana mutating twice next turn.

rows.name: Swan Song
rows.text: one mana for the removal spell or wrath aimed at the pile.

rows.name: An Offer You Can't Refuse
rows.text: the same, and their two Treasures matter less than your pile surviving.

rows.name: Ivy, Gleeful Spellthief
rows.text: copies any single-target spell — theirs or yours — onto herself. She steals removal and doubles pumps.

rows.name: Portal to Phyrexia
rows.text: three creatures gone from every opponent, then a reanimation every upkeep.

rows.name: Craterhoof Behemoth
rows.text: even a modest board plus one enormous trampling pile is lethal to the table.

rows.name: Titan of Industry
rows.text: two modes on entry, and the shield counter protects the pile from the removal spell it was going to die to.

rows.name: Etali, Primal Conqueror

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a hexproof one-drop and a mutate creature. Slippery Bogle on turn one into a mutate on turn two is the start that makes the deck's engine turn on before anyone can interact.
Do not mutate onto Animar unless you have to. He is the discount engine, and putting him under a pile risks losing him to the removal spell aimed at the whole thing.

Order the pile with the TOP card in mind. The creature on top decides the name, power, toughness and — importantly — whether it flies and tramples. Illuna and Sawtusk Demolisher on top attack well; Porcuparrot on top does not.

rows.name: Auspicious Starrix
rows.text: mutate it EARLY and keep mutating onto that pile. Its count is per-Starrix, so a Starrix that has mutated four times puts four free permanents onto the battlefield the next time.
